Unauthorized Device Registration [Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-287] on IoT Core, IoT Device Management, Certificate Manager, DynamoDB Device Registry Table: An attacker could attempt to register unauthorized devices by intercepting the device registration process or compromising the certificate provisioning workflow. An attacker registers a malicious device using stolen or forged certificates, gaining access to send data into the system and potentially exfiltrate information about other

Insecure Data Storage in S3 [Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-284] on S3 Bucket (LongTermStorageBucket), Processing Lambda, QuickSight: While the bucket has S3-managed encryption and public access blocking, IAM roles or bucket policies might grant excessive permissions to internal users or services. An unauthorized internal user with overly permissive IAM permissions could access sensitive IoT data stored in the S3 bucket, leading to data breach.

Insufficient Monitoring and Alerting [Repudiation, Information Disclosure, CWE-223] on CloudWatch, SNS Alerts, IoT Core, Lambda Functions, Kinesis Data Stream: Lack of comprehensive monitoring could allow attackers to perform malicious activities without detection. An attacker compromises a device or gains unauthorized access to AWS resources, and their activities go unnoticed due to insufficient monitoring.

Insecure Lambda Function Configuration [Elevation of Privilege, Tampering, CWE-272] on Processing Lambda, Notification Lambda, Update Lambda, IAM Roles: Lambda functions with overly permissive IAM roles could be exploited to access or modify data they shouldn't have access to. An attacker exploits a vulnerability in the Processing Lambda to gain access to sensitive data in DynamoDB or modify device state information.

Denial of Service Through Message Flooding [Denial of Service, CWE-400] on IoT Core, Kinesis Data Stream, Processing Lambda, DynamoDB Tables: Attackers could flood the system with messages from compromised devices or through replay attacks. Multiple compromised devices send an excessive number of messages, overwhelming Kinesis streams and downstream processing capabilities.

Insufficient Access Control for Data Visualization [Information Disclosure, CWE-284] on QuickSight, Timestream, S3 Bucket: Lack of proper access controls in QuickSight could allow users to view data from devices or organizations they shouldn't have access to. An employee views sensitive IoT data from other departments or organizations through improperly configured QuickSight dashboards.
